solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spectral cat behind ventilator, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the cat sits behind the ventilator, so its word follows the other in the answer
says the word we build is only heard, so its spelling can differ from what we say

parts.note: a fan is a ventilator; spelt here to match the sound
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A ghostly cat lurking behind a ventilator, heard rather than seen.
explanation.walkthrough: FAN TOM said aloud is PHANTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost, and 'spectral' is used as an adjective of a ghostly thing, as in 'phantom limb' — attributive noun use.

clue.text: Paper strip for nutritious snack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the comic strip by Charles Schulz printed in newspapers
second meaning: groundnuts eaten as a snack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper strip' suggests a sliver of paper; it is a newspaper comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both Schulz's long-running newspaper cartoon and the protein-rich legume people nibble.

clue.text: Various fallen Roman ruins

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Assorted broken-down remains of the Roman world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruins' reads as a noun, but it is the verb that tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All manner of' is an idiom meaning many different kinds, a close match for various.

clue.text: Extremely tricky ruse to secure Oscar for Citizen Kane?

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of tricky

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a con is a trick or ruse
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A cunning plan to win the Academy Award for Orson Welles's film.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the film winning an Oscar; but Charles Foster Kane, the character, is the definition, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Kane, the hero of Citizen Kane, is a newspaper magnate, an example of a business mogul.

clue.text: Woman's first entitlement could be over before term

indicators.note: before places one word in front of the other

parts.note: a maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A woman's earliest right may have lapsed before the school term began.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a maiden over is one from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's surname before marriage is her original one, the first she was entitled to.

clue.text: Stout pin in the form of catch on the hotplate

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it in the reading order

parts.note: a hob is the hotplate on top of a cooker
to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: a thick pin used as a catch on the cooker's hotplate.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobnail is a short nail with a large head, a sturdy pin hammered into boot soles.

clue.text: Native dance from Haiti originally, with alias

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the start of the word

parts.note: first letter of Haiti
AKA, also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: An indigenous dance that originated in Haiti, going under another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haiti' points to the Caribbean, but the dance is Maori from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the ceremonial war dance of the Maori people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Aristo's taken up residence across island for warmth

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nob is an upper-class person

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides

parts.note: a home is a residence
I is an abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A posh person moves into a home on an island to enjoy its warm climate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a joining word. 'Warmth' hints at climate; it is warmth of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness, the warmth of a good-natured person.

clue.text: Not quite top primate

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the apex is the top

explanation.surface: A primate that falls just short of the top of the hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes such as gorillas and chimpanzees belong to the order of primates.

clue.text: Noblewoman always accepts old penny when rent's traditionally due

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a lady is a noblewoman
ay (aye) is an old word for always, as in 'for ay'
d was the symbol for a pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: An aristocrat always takes a penny on rent day.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Day, 25 March, is the Feast of the Annunciation and an English quarter day, when rents fell due.
explanation.definitionFit: As one of the quarter days of the English calendar, it was the traditional date for paying rent.

clue.text: Tool's completely articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all wrong'

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a tool has been fully jointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' looks like it means jointed, as in an articulated lorry; here it means pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool used for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Small contribution from cowardly US agent pocketing key

parts.note: chicken means cowardly

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in US slang
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A timid American agent offers a paltry sum, hiding a key in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken feed is an idiom for a trivially small amount of money.

clue.text: A French bible translation outstanding? That's not acknowledged

parts.note: un is French for a
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
an outstanding debt is one still owed

explanation.surface: An excellent French Bible translation goes uncredited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellence; it means unpaid. The Authorized Version is the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to admit openly, so something unavowed has never been admitted or owned up to.

clue.text: Benefit received by industrial carrier put up

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so it goes inside the other word

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
use, as in 'of some use', is benefit

explanation.surface: A payment from a freight company gets put up for others to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up is to give them lodging, which is to house them.

clue.text: Religious work marshals bars at Tate Modern's opening

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of modern

explanation.surface: A sacred work bans people from the bars at the Tate Modern gallery's launch.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is London's modern art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stabat Mater is a medieval Latin hymn set to music by many composers, a piece of sacred music.

clue.text: Military leader coming forth with great weight

parts.note: welling is flowing out or coming forth
a ton is a great weight

explanation.surface: A general stepping forward to speak with great authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight' suggests influence; it is a literal heavy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington was the British general who beat Napoleon at Waterloo.

clue.text: Decline suitable place for washing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go down or deteriorate
second meaning: a basin with taps in a kitchen

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an appropriate spot to do the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to fall or drop; as a noun it is the basin used for washing up.

clue.text: Popular titbit's bad taste

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a delicacy is a choice morsel of food

explanation.surface: A fashionable snack turns out to have a nasty flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taste' invites a food reading; it is taste as in manners.
explanation.definitionFit: An indelicacy is a coarse or tactless remark or act, a lapse in refinement.

clue.text: Bargained for stock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: anticipated, as in 'more than I bargained for'
second meaning: standard or predictable, as in a stock reply

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests goods or shares to bargain over; it is the adjective meaning usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anticipated has been bargained for, and a stock answer is the predictable, foreseen one.

clue.text: Pro formerly on the plump side, say

parts.note: pro means in favour of
ex means former, as in ex-wife
ample describes a generously rounded figure

explanation.surface: A former professional who has put on a little weight, someone might say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' at the end looks like a soundalike signal or a mere example marker, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, exactly as the phrase 'for instance' does.

clue.text: Empty fruitful land Open University's invested in

parts.note: fat land is fertile, fruitful land

indicators.note: something invested in is placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the US is a land, a country
OU is the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: Productive farmland has been bought by a distance-learning university, pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' suggests money; here it simply means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatuous means silly and pointless, as in an empty or vacuous remark.

clue.text: Shakes containers

definitions.meaning: second meaning: glass pots with lids

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to jolt unpleasantly; as a plural noun it means glass storage vessels.

clue.text: Pastry daughter in Ulster cooked?

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
cooked means altered by preparation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
D is an abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl in Northern Ireland baked some pastry, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered pastry, usually filled with apple, from Austria.

clue.text: Damp food raised problem for marsupial

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Soggy food has become an issue for a pouched animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is a tree-dwelling marsupial of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Mother's third of payment for sweet

indicators.note: the third means we keep just the letter in third place of that word

parts.note: third letter of mother
taken as written
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A third of mum's payment goes on confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a third of a payment; in fact only the third letter of mother is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter, a classic British sweet.

clue.text: Nark monarch after playing well

indicators.note: the monarch's word comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: a player in form is playing well
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A police spy keeps watch on a sovereign who has been performing well.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark passes information to the police, which is what an informer does.

clue.text: Constant torture ruled out on a regular basis

indicators.text: ruled out on a regular basis
indicators.note: letters struck out at regular intervals leave every other one standing

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of torture

explanation.surface: Persistent torture is being banned at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean loyal and steadfast, as in a constant friend.

clue.text: Takes out alumnus and scholarly son

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
literate means well read
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A former student and his bookish son go out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes out' suggests escorting someone; it means destroys.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a target is to wipe it out completely, which is to obliterate it.

clue.text: National leaders from Levant and Orient

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so we take the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letter of Levant
first letter of and
first letter of Orient

explanation.surface: Heads of state from the Middle and Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective; it is the noun for a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lao is a native or citizen of Laos, in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Delinquent's obligation to return missing book

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters are read right to left
missing means something is absent, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a debt is an obligation
B is an abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A young offender has to give back an overdue library book.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes, seen as a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Teds were the original British youth tearaways, so the word serves for a juvenile delinquent.

clue.text: Foot is special on tailless ungulates

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
taken as written
deer are hoofed mammals

explanation.surface: A hoof is something special on animals that have lost their tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like part of the animal picture, but here it is a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot is a metrical unit, and a spondee is one made of two stressed syllables.

clue.text: Learn unexpectedly about doubtful expression for DCI perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters surrounds the other
something unexpected comes out differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
um is a hesitant sound of doubt

explanation.surface: Being told unexpectedly about a vague remark concerning a detective chief inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: DCI reads as a Detective Chief Inspector, but here it is Roman 601.
explanation.definitionFit: DCI in Roman figures stands for 601, so it is one example of a number symbol.
